walkthroughs.body_html:
Engaging with Anthropological Material — a core area of Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Engaging with Anthropological Material brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Engaging with Anthropological Material.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: C. Wright Mills published 'The Sociological Imagination' in:

options: Marx
Weber
Comte
Durkheim
Secret lessons teachers deliberately hide from students.
The unspoken norms, values, and behaviours taught implicitly in schools.
Because they hate qualitative research.
Topics removed from the syllabus.

mcqs.q: Why do positivists prefer quantitative methods?
options: Acts are objectively deviant regardless of context.
They produce objective, reliable, generalisable data resembling natural science.
Because they hate qualitative research.
Because numbers are easier to collect than words.

mcqs.q: According to Becker, what makes an act deviant?
options: Breaking a law makes any act deviant.
Acts are objectively deviant regardless of context.
Being labelled as deviant by others - deviance is in the reaction, not the act.
Because they hate qualitative research.
